clue.text: Grain coming from a tropic island

indicators.note: here the grain is taken away out of the tropic's name, so coming from means removed

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is one of the two tropics
corn is a general word for grain

explanation.surface: Someone harvesting cereal on a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' signals removal: take CORN out of CAPRICORN, leaving CAPRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian isle in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Arms displayed in a hostile way?

definitions.text: Arms displayed in a hostile way?

parts.words: Arms displayed in a hostile way?
parts.note: not weapons brandished but a confrontational stance with hands on hips and elbows sticking out

explanation.surface: Weapons being brandished menacingly.
explanation.definitionFit: The posture with hands on hips and elbows bent outward often looks aggressive or defiant.

clue.text: Is inquisitive about the tank and soldiers

indicators.note: the prying word goes round the container word, so about signals surrounding

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy, so 'is inquisitive' gives pries
a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: Someone nosing around an army tank and its crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tank' suggests the military vehicle, but it is the brewing VAT, held 'about' by PRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates are the lowest-ranking soldiers in an army.

clue.text: Give a hoot!

parts.note: read not as 'care' but literally: make a howling call like an owl

explanation.surface: A slangy exhortation to care about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To howl or wail with a hooting cry, as owls and mourners do.

clue.text: Novelist to drink without something to eat

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the drinking word goes around the food word

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
a bread roll is something to eat

explanation.surface: A writer drinking on an empty stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: TOPE wraps ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist, author of the Barchester novels.

clue.text: Shame! Don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: disgrace or dishonour, as a noun
an order to doubt or reject something as untrue

explanation.surface: Two indignant exclamations at a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means disgrace; as a verb it means to refuse to credit a claim.

clue.text: Punishment escaped by unnamed soldiers

parts.note: alludes to the saying 'no names, no ...': if nobody is named, nobody can be punished with this military drill

explanation.surface: Anonymous troops dodging a disciplinary sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'no names, no pack drill' means nobody named, nobody punished.
explanation.definitionFit: A military punishment of marching up and down in full kit.

clue.text: A girl in distress sought by Lohengrin

indicators.note: distressed letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress, as in a knightly romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is a knight of the Holy Grail in the Arthurian legend and in Wagner's opera.

clue.text: People go crazy running it

parts.note: refers to the idiom about running wild in a frenzy, rather than running a business

explanation.surface: Managing something drives its staff mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To 'run' this word is to rampage out of control.

clue.text: It's so ancient it sounds like original sin!

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is pronounced like the phrase that follows

parts.note: the first, primary wrong: a prime evil

explanation.surface: A joke that the oldest wrongdoing gives its name to great age.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval things belong to the earliest ages of the world.

clue.text: Ill-will of many to a girl

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A crowd bearing a grudge against a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or the wish to do harm.

clue.text: Left or right in the vessel

definitions.text: Left or right in the vessel

parts.words: Left or right in the vessel
parts.note: looks like a choice of directions, but aboard ship the left-hand side has its own name

explanation.surface: Asking which way to turn on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for the left side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: An absorbing business transaction

parts.note: absorbing means not gripping but swallowing up: one company absorbs another

explanation.surface: A fascinating commercial deal.
explanation.definitionFit: One firm buying control of another, swallowing it up.

clue.text: It's often taken up by winter sportsman

definitions.text: It's often taken up by winter sportsman

parts.words: It's often taken up by winter sportsman
parts.note: taken up suggests adopting a hobby, but here it is the seat carrying a skier uphill

explanation.surface: Talking about a pastime popular with skiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable-hung seat that carries skiers up a mountain slope.

clue.text: Greek character possibly seen as Oriental

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the following word may possibly be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A Greek person who might be mistaken for an Asian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SEEN into NESE, after CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from China, a country of the Orient.

clue.text: Gives information which could lead to making an arrest

indicators.note: the clue words could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police informer whose tip-off results in an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or tell a story is to pass on information.

clue.text: One is going to say it

definitions.text: One is going to say it

parts.words: One is going to say it
parts.note: not 'about to speak' but 'one who is leaving' says this farewell

explanation.surface: Someone about to make a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British word for goodbye.

clue.text: Public building was due to be consecrated

parts.note: a hall is a building for public gatherings
owed means was due to be paid

explanation.surface: A town hall about to be made sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: Made holy or sanctified.

clue.text: Sweetheart lost by doctor and poet

indicators.note: the doctor drops a letter, so lost by marks a removal

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A doctor who is also a poet, jilted in love.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSEMAN is the British term for a junior hospital doctor; remove E to leave the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman wrote the verse cycle A Shropshire Lad.

clue.text: A noted text-book

parts.note: noted reads as famous, but means set to musical notes: the words of an opera

explanation.surface: A famous school book.
explanation.definitionFit: The written words of an opera or musical, printed as a booklet.

clue.text: They are nailed on the foot

definitions.text: They are nailed on the foot

parts.words: They are nailed on the foot
parts.note: nailed suggests hammering, but these digits simply have toenails

explanation.surface: Horseshoes being fixed on a hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits of the foot each bear a nail.

clue.text: The French way to get fat

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: How French people put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Kick into wind again

definitions.meaning: the backward jolt of a gun when fired
to coil once more, as a rope or spring

explanation.surface: A gun's jolt as the wind changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's backward jerk; also, read as re-coil, to loop something round a second time.

clue.text: Publish and I p-prosecute!

parts.note: the stammer shows a doubled first letter, and to prosecute is to sue, so a stammered sue

explanation.surface: A stammering threat to take a publisher to court.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'p-prosecute' shows a stammer; transfer it to SUE, giving S-SUE after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring out a book or magazine for the public.

clue.text: Lorraine's companion

parts.note: Lorraine looks like a woman's name, but it is a French region paired with its neighbour

explanation.surface: Asking about a woman's friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The French region that is always paired with Lorraine, as in the two provinces lost to Germany in 1871.

clue.text: Owes cash for the display cabinet

indicators.note: the letters are exchanged for a new arrangement, so for signals the anagram here

explanation.surface: Someone in debt over a glass display unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-fronted case for exhibiting objects.

clue.text: Frequently expressed as decimal

definitions.meaning: read as two words: ..., as decimals are fractions ...

explanation.surface: How often a number is given as a decimal.
explanation.definitionFit: Many times; split into two words it gives the base of the decimal system.

clue.text: Disagreeing about point, tongue-in-cheek

indicators.note: the disagreeing word goes around the point, so about means surrounding

parts.note: factious means given to dissent and squabbling
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a point, not meant seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Joking or flippant, not intended seriously.
